identification: Two trays of loose paper ephemera: a hand-coloured engraved antique map 'Britannia Saxonica' (Saxon England, likely 18th c.), several Tasmanian/Victorian cabinet card photographs including Louis Konrad of 60 Cameron St Launceston (c1895-1905, two girls) and a Newman cabinet card, a wedding photo, a mill/watermill photo, a rural settlement panorama photograph, a N.J. Caire (Melbourne) Fitzroy Gardens 'Many Happy Returns of the Day' card, 19th c. chromolithograph botanical plates (bromeliad, white blossom) and a modern-looking botanical print of Eucalyptus coccifera (Tasmanian snow gum), plus invitation cards and general ephemera.

viewing_check: Map first: measure the full sheet (43 x 37 or 47 x 39 cm), paper and margins, any verso text. Then the panorama (place name on back or margin), the 'ERBY' sheet, the group photo and mill photo (captions), the letters (writers), the plastic sleeves (open them), and every botanical print for plate captions.
